messages:
maria: Heads up — we just paused the kernel-selector rollout (canary) for v0.9.7. Observed sudden KV-cache fragmentation + OOMs on longctx endpoints during a chat load. Holding the rollout.

alex: What do the logs/metrics show? p95 mem, eviction churn?

maria: p95 memory jumped ~2.1x right after the kernel-router change. Eviction churn up, slab fragmentation index spiked. Repro locally with seqlen=2048 workload.

jin: pinging @kyle for infra traces. Do we have a CI perf job that covers longctx workloads? :eyes: 

kyle: Running the perf CI sweep now. Preliminary traces show alternating kernel choices every other request which seems to interleave alloc patterns -> fragmentation. Suspect kernel-routing heuristic change in commit 9f3a2b7.

maria: Added a tiny repro command below, run locally on a dev instance (will reproduce flaky OOM):

```
./tools/run_longctx_repro --model llama2 --seq-len 2048 --concurrency 8 --kernel=auto
```

alex: Can we force a stable kernel (e.g., kernel=stable-gemm) to confirm?

maria: Forcing stable kernel removes the OOMs in the repro. Rolling rollback for canary and opening a deploy revert.

deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated for cluster-usa-east-1 by maria at 1964001237 :white_check_mark:

jin: I'll run a commit search over the kernel-router changes tonight. Keeping canary paused until we have a root cause.

kyle: I added temporary runtime metrics: kernel-flips/sec and slab-frag-index to the dashboard. Also toggled KV-cache eviction to be a bit more aggressive on the paused canary nodes as a short-term mitigation.

alex: Great. Please post the perf CI link and a short checklist for the incident note.

maria: Perf CI run: https://ci.redwood-internal/runs/2491 — shows mem spike at test 7 where kernel switch happens. Opening incident note now.

ashley: FYI this only hit a subfleet with A100 instances (a100-smi). Could be a hardware/kernel-codepath interaction.

jin: If it's A100-specific, the kernel selection path might choose different kernels per compute capability. I'm adding a hardware matrix to the repro (cc @maria).

maria: Next steps: (1) rollback canary — done, (2) repro with stable kernel — confirmed no OOM, (3) commit-level search on kernel-router (jin), (4) decide on revert vs. patching kernel-router heuristic. I'll update this thread with findings. :memo:

kyle: Thumbs up. If we need an emergency revert to v0.9.6, ping infra on-call.

maria: tagging ops-oncall @sre to keep in the loop.

sre-bot: oncall notified: @sre_team. Acknowledge if you need help.

maria: Thanks everyone, will post bisect results and a short mitigation plan later today.
